uncited: - A set of rays, each defined by an origin $\mathbf{o}_{i,j}$ and direction $\mathbf{d}_{ray}$.
Each element at index $k = i + j \cdot W$ stores a 2D screen coordinate normalized to $[-1, 1]$ for $x$ and $y$, with $z=0$.
For each pixel $(i, j)$, cast a ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o}_{i,j} + t \cdot \mathbf{d}_{ray}$ into the volume data.
- If $\mathbf{M}$ is singular or degenerate, the cross product may yield a zero vector.
- The normalization to $[-1, 1]$ assumes a centered projection plane.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(W \cdot H)$ to generate all ray origins and directions.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(W \cdot H)$ to store the origins and directions.
The direction computation is constant time per ray (all rays share the same direction in orthographic mode).
- **When to use:** Isometric views, technical visualizations, voxel rendering where perspective is not desired.
- **When not to use:** Perspective views, scenes requiring depth-based field of view.
